periods.analysis: Pipeline Renewal is green at 10% complete, establishing the baseline for this eight-quarter run; there is no prior supplied quarter to calculate movement against. Phase 1 — citywide pipe condition assessment, Phase 2 — Maple St corridor replacement, and Phase 3 contractor procurement are complete, which means the paper is not ahead of the pipe for once. The Phase 3 pipe-cohort condition survey remains in-progress with dueOffsetDays 4, focused on the 1970s cast-iron runs tagged HV-WM-14C, HV-WM-22A, and the Harbor Boulevard pressure-zone laterals. Phase 3 construction start is still not-started with dueOffsetDays 60, and the FY27 pipeline funding request to council is not-started with dueOffsetDays 150, so the serious water-main risk is being managed but not wished away.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green status by closing the Phase 3 pipe-cohort condition survey within the 4-day window and loading the CCTV, leak-log, and soil-corrosion scores into the asset register before crews price work packages. Have Crew 7 and the on-call utility locator pre-walk Maple-to-Harbor tie-ins so the Phase 3 construction start can move cleanly when the 60-day mark arrives. Start the FY27 council funding file now with break history, pipe age, and avoided-emergency-repair costs; an AA-rated city should defend the ask with evidence, not adjectives.

Draft the FY27 funding request outline with asset IDs, break counts, and preliminary unit costs so council sees the pipe problem in feet, dollars, and risk.

The Phase 3 pipe-cohort condition survey remains in-progress with dueOffsetDays 4, and the last checks are centered on older cast-iron near the marina where salt exposure has never been kind to metal. Advance the FY27 funding request to a finance-review draft and tie it to Harborview's AA bond discipline: renew the worst pipe before it becomes the most expensive pipe.

periods.analysis: Pipeline Renewal increased from 35% to 40% complete, a quarter-over-quarter gain of 5 percentage points, and remains green. The same milestone structure is holding: Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3 contractor procurement are complete; the Phase 3 pipe-cohort condition survey is in-progress with dueOffsetDays 4; Phase 3 construction start is not-started with dueOffsetDays 60; and the FY27 pipeline funding request is not-started with dueOffsetDays 150. Wet-weather response this quarter showed why we keep pushing: saturated soils around HV-WM-14C increase consequence even when the break count is being actively managed. The pipes do not read our calendar, so the green status is earned only if the next 60 days stay operational, not ceremonial.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the green by issuing a 30/60-day readiness checklist that names the crew lead, inspector, shutdown window, traffic control route, and material lot for each Phase 3 segment. Extend the program by adding wet-weather contingency language to the contractor notice-to-proceed package, including trench dewatering and steel-plate response times. Put the FY27 funding request into executive review with the break-risk map, because that is the cleanest way to turn condition data into a defensible capital decision.
